reframe.previous_center: bounded agent authority as a defensive architecture
reframe.research_question: Can developers reason about an agent's effective authority more reliably when that authority is materialized as an inspectable, diffable object?
reframe.kill_criterion: If the materialized checkout tells a developer nothing useful beyond what the underlying policy and entitlement configuration already tells them, the project is only a visualization layer and should be narrowed or stopped.

not_claimed: This automatically derives perfect least privilege.
This is a new security primitive.
This replaces IAM, capability systems, policy engines, sandboxes or reference monitors.
This introduces novel out-of-model enforcement; deterministic external enforcement is established prior art.
This can literally snapshot all external reality.
This addresses infrastructure-level sandbox escape or credential harvesting by itself.
This would have prevented the July 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face incident.

canonical_state.description: Authoritative application and organizational state outside the model.

projection.description: The checkout-like, inspectable materialization exposed for a task.

effect_gate.description: A live authorization path for consequential actions; deliberately not treated as a checkout or merge operation.

pause_authority.description: The explicit ability to halt, suspend or revoke an agent's runtime authority, including who may invoke it and through which path.
questions: Can automated monitoring invoke a pause directly?
What authority is revoked when paused?

delegation.description: Authority propagation across agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool chains.
delegation.status: early research candidate rather than late roadmap item
questions: What authority narrowed or expanded at each hop?
Who is attributable for the final effect?
Can the complete chain be inspected as one object or trace?

first_demo.agent_behavior: hardcoded first so the representation can be tested independently from model variability; optional LLM second

layout.left: current checkout: resources, capabilities, provenance, expiry
layout.right: agent transcript or attempted action sequence

first_demo.first_measure: Can a developer explain what changed in effective authority from the checkout diff without reading the underlying policy implementation?

july_2026_openai_hugging_face.relevance: inspiration and boundary lesson, not a claimed prevented incident
july_2026_openai_hugging_face.verified_lesson: The incident crossed infrastructure trust boundaries through sandbox escape, exposed execution paths, credentials and lateral movement. Authority Checkout currently models an application/runtime authority representation above those infrastructure controls.
transferable_questions: What ambient authority exists outside the model-visible checkout?
Who can pause automated work after monitoring detects danger?

success_criteria.primary: The checkout representation exposes effective authority in a way that is materially easier to inspect, compare and explain than the policy inputs alone.
success_criteria.secondary: Delegation, expiry and authority changes can be represented without implying enforcement guarantees the prototype does not provide.
success_criteria.documentation: Every reframe preserves the assumption that failed, the evidence that challenged it and the resulting design change.
